Interpretation: the critical line turns two zero configurations into direction-sensitive weighted masses, permitting comparison without locating individual zeros. parents.title: Gamma-factor derivatives and sublinear singular integrals control the functional-equation transfer

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source fact: in any fixed vertical strip and at sufficiently large height, chi^(m)(s)/chi(s) has dominant size (-log|t|)^m with one lower logarithmic order of error. This yields eventual absence of zeros and poles for chi derivatives there. A separately cited lemma bounds the L^p integral, 0<p<1, of sums of shifted reciprocal terms. Interpretation: the first two lemmas neutralize new gamma-factor singularities under differentiation, while the third turns local pole terms into an integrable aggregate; together they prepare a functional-equation transfer without counting zeta zeros themselves. Boundary: Lemmas 1-2 are proved here, Lemma 3 is imported, and all uniform claims retain their fixed-strip, high-height scope.

parents.title: Differentiate the functional equation, apply Littlewood, and telescope logarithmic derivatives

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source fact: differentiating the functional equation factors reflected derivative zeros through an auxiliary J_m. Littlewood's lemma then converts their horizontal displacement into a boundary integral of J_m/zeta. To control that integral, the proof bounds fractional moments of zeta^(j)/zeta by factoring them into successive derivative ratios, applying local partial fractions, a derivative zero-count estimate, the cited sublinear L^p lemma, and Holder's inequality. Interpretation: reflection changes a left-zero problem into an auxiliary zero problem, Littlewood changes zero geometry into boundary size, and telescoping reduces a high derivative ratio to adjacent ratios with local control. Boundary: the result is aggregate and inherits cited zero-count and partial-fraction inputs.

parents.title: A length-T^(4/7) mollified mean square becomes a zero-counting instrument

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source fact: Conrey's cited theorem evaluates the mean square of V(s)B(s) on a shifted critical line, where B is a Mobius-polynomial mollifier of length T^theta with theta<4/7 and V is a polynomial differential operator applied to zeta. The asymptotic constant c(P,Q,R) is an explicit double integral. Interpretation: the theorem replaces pointwise cancellation by an averaged quadratic cost whose dependence on P, Q, and R exposes a variational choice of mollifier shape and derivative combination. Boundary: this span imports the Kloosterman-sum machinery and the mean-square formula alone proves no zero proportion; that requires later zero-counting arguments.

parents.title: Jensen plus an optimized sinh mollifier gives the right-side derivative-zero proportion

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source fact: Littlewood's lemma and Jensen bound derivative zeros on or left of the critical line by a mollified mean square of J_k. Integration by parts replaces J_k by the differential operator V_k with Q_k(x)=(1-x)^k, so Conrey's theorem supplies c(P,Q_k,R). Approximating a continuous sinh profile by admissible polynomials and optimizing its parameter makes the infimum of c approach 2, yielding a right-side lower density approaching one with k. Interpretation: a zero count is converted into a variational cost, and concentration of Q_k makes the large-order optimization tractable. Boundary: the sinh profile represents an infimum rather than a literal admissible polynomial, and the conclusion is a density bound, not pointwise location.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Identifies the admissible relaxation and the sequence of transformations from zero geometry to an explicit functional, including what the optimization does not prove.

parents.title: A xi-plus-derivative combination counts excess multiplicity and bounds distinct zeros

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source fact: the auxiliary function f built from xi and xi' is not zero at a simple xi zero, while a zero of multiplicity r survives with multiplicity r-1. Symmetry and Littlewood therefore make zeros of f control N(T)-N_d(T). Jensen reduces the problem to a mollified mean square; rewriting f through a linear differential polynomial Q and importing Conrey's optimized parameters with Q(0)=1 gives kappa_d>0.70. Interpretation: f removes exactly one layer of vanishing, turning excess multiplicity into a zero set accessible to averaged estimates. Boundary: the construction bounds a distinct-zero proportion; it neither locates zeros nor proves simplicity, and Q(0)=1 restricts the admissible optimization.
